newsitem.title: USA: LaGrange lock on Illinois River reopens - officials.
newsitem.headline: LaGrange lock on Illinois River reopens - officials.

text.p: The LaGrange lock on the Illinois River was reopened late Thursday after an underwater hyraulic lead had kept the lock closed since Wednesday, a U.S. Army Corp of Engineers official said.
All traffic north and south of the lock had been halted since Wednesday.
"We opened the lock at 1415 CST on Thursday and normal operations resumed," U.S. Army Corps of Engineers chief of maintenance Mike Zerbonia said.
A underwater hydraulic leak shut down the lock near Beardstown, Ill., and held up about 18 tows with 216 barges on Thursday, Lockmaster Stan Wallace said.
On Friday, tow boats were still waiting to get through.

"Right now, we got 20 tows sitting here with 152 loaded barges and 93 empty barges," Wallace said. "December, January and February are our busiest times of the year. In December, 1995, we locked 436 tows here."
But ice floes on the Illinois River from the current bitter cold temperatures could slow down barge traffic.

"We may see some restrictions on tow size as early as today (Friday)," Wallace said. "I would suspect that sometime over the weekend we would end up with 70-foot tow width restrictions due to the icy conditions."
Elsewhere on the Illinois River, barges were moving.
"As the ice thickens, the tows will have to be moving slower and may have to get help from other tow boats to push them through the ice on parts of the Illinois," Zerbonia said.

Ken Kruchowski, spokesman with the U.S. Army Corps of engineers, St Louis district, said as of early Friday, there were no traffic problems from Lock and Dam 22 near Saverton, Mo., to Locks 27 near Granite City, Ill.
There were repairs scheduled at Lock and Dam 24, at Clarksville, Mo., and they will not be finished until early February, he said.

"That has closed Lock and Dam 24 during the daytime hours from 6.00 AM to 6.00 PM CST," Kruchowski said. "Lock and Dam 25, near Winfield, Mo., is also having repair work done but that has not affected barge traffic."

Ron Fournier, chief of public affairs, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Rock Island District, Ill., said the navigation industry has basically stopped shipping in the middle of December from Lock and Dam 19, at Keokuk, Iowa, to Minneapolis. "They do this in expectation of poor shipping conditions during the winter months," Fournier said.
